_comment: EXAMPLE. Copy to model_routes.json and edit — the real file is gitignored,
like .env. The INTERNAL NAMES are the repo's contract: agent_configs and the
vision gate reference `flash` / `pro` / `glm` / `smart` / `vision`, so those
keys must exist. WHICH endpoints serve them is entirely yours — the lists
below are one operator's answer, not a requirement.
Internal model name -> ordered list of concrete provider/model endpoints.
An agent_config's `model` (and the vision gate's judge) names one of these;
AIGateway binds the first candidate and falls over to the next ONLY on an
endpoint error (401/403 dead key or lapsed plan, 429 quota/rate limit, 5xx,
connection loss). A bad request or an oversized context is NOT failed over
— every candidate would reject it the same way.
STICKY, never round-robin: a gateway lives for one step, so all of that
step's turns hit one endpoint. Provider prefix caches are per-provider and
this workload is 26:1 prefill:decode at an 89.4% hit rate; alternating
endpoints per call converts cached input into full-price input and costs
more than any token plan saves. Spread quota per RUN, not per call.
A spent usage window parks that ONE provider/model until the provider's
stated reset instant, so the plans below are consumed in order and a spent
one is skipped outright rather than re-probed once per step.
Providers referenced here must exist in llm_providers.json, and their key
must be mounted in docker-compose.yml's `secrets:` block. Names not listed
here pass through unchanged if they contain a '/', so a concrete
provider/model still works in an agent_config with no entry.
_ordering_note: Every route ends with a `deepseek/` PAY-AS-YOU-GO candidate on purpose. A
token plan can run out; pay-as-you-go cannot, so it is the only thing that
makes 'both plans are spent' a slowdown instead of a stop. ark and qwen are
separate plans with separate windows, so they are consumed in order and a
spent one is parked, not re-probed.
How much a failover changes, per route:
* flash / pro — NOTHING but the bill. Same model, different door. (Caveat:
qwen serves DATED snapshots, deepseek-v4-flash-0731, where ark serves a
rolling alias; they can drift when DeepSeek ships a new snapshot.)
* glm — degrades. 5.2 is genuinely older than 5.3, and the last candidate
* smart / vision — a different model outright. See their notes.
So `served_by` in the trace is not bookkeeping: for three of the five routes
it is what tells you whether a result is evidence about the model you think
_glm_note: The last candidate is a DIFFERENT FAMILY, not another door to GLM. That is
a real behaviour change and it is the point: without it, both token plans
running out leaves every glm role with nowhere to go and the run stops. A
DeepSeek answer is a worse GLM answer than GLM's; it is a far better one
than no answer. Check `served_by` in the trace before reading a glm-role
_smart_note: qwen3.8-max: a 2.4T MoE (95B active), 262K context, native vision, its own
low/medium/xhigh effort scale. NOT interchangeable with the others, so it
is its own route and no existing role has been moved onto it.
What the independent evidence supports (Aug 2026): elite ALGORITHMIC coding
and tool use (LMArena Code #3), GPQA reproduced at 92.6% vs a claimed 92.7%.
What it does NOT support: the agentic numbers. Terminal-Bench 2.1 does not
replicate under a neutral harness, it sits #15/55 on the Coding Agent Index
with an 11-point SWE-bench gap to Opus 5, and agentic coding is its worst
LiveBench category. It is also reported unreliable on facts, and to
'default to wildly overthinking' — pin the effort if you use it.
Read against this pipeline: that profile fits the ONE-SHOT judgement steps
(the *_review reviewers, the architect, the PM) and argues AGAINST t_impl,
which is a 24-turn agentic tool loop — its worst category — and against the
researcher, which must not invent facts. Measure before moving any role:
replay the step against ~/.AItelier/scratch/effort_ab/ rather than trusting
this paragraph.
The fallbacks are a DIFFERENT model, so a failover here changes behaviour,
not just the bill. That is the right trade for availability, but it means a
run served by the fallback is not evidence about qwen3.8-max — check
`served_by` in the trace before drawing a conclusion.
_vision_note: The judge for the Godot readability gate (aitelier/tools/godot_vision).
Put a self-hosted vision endpoint FIRST if you have one — it is free and the
gate is the heaviest consumer of frames. Register it in llm_providers.json
and prepend it here; the example lists public endpoints only.
Every candidate must accept IMAGE input, and that is the one capability a
text smoke test cannot see: verified 2026-08-25, Ark's plan serves
deepseek-v4-flash-vision-exp for TEXT and refuses images. POST a real frame
before adding a candidate; do not read a model card.
The frame-batching budget does NOT follow the candidate — it stays
GODOT_VISION_CONTEXT_TOKENS. Sizing batches to whichever judge happened to
answer would make the batch layout, and thus which frames are compared
against each other, depend on an infra accident.
